title: Harcourt Trophies Grade 2-1 End-of-Selection Tests — Vocab, Comprehension & Writing
callouts: assessments broken up into vocab, comprehension and writing sections

vocabulary.structure: Sentence with blank → pick from 4 options (A/B/C/D). Items 1-6 are multiple choice, items 19-20 are written response.

comprehension.structure: Questions 7-18 are multiple choice (4 options). Questions 19-20 are open-response (write the answer on lines).

writing.structure: Questions 19-20: open-ended prompts with 2-3 lines for response. Requires recall + personal connection.

vocabulary.structure: Same format as Frog and Toad — sentence context + 4 options

writing.structure: Questions 19-20 open-ended with 2-3 lines. Example: 'Name two foods that you can make with apples.'

overallLayout.visualHierarchy: text-only — clean section headers (Vocabulary / Comprehension bold), no illustrations

appealDrivers: clean uncluttered layout keeps focus on comprehension, not decoration

threePartAssessmentStructure.description: Every end-of-selection test follows the same three-part structure: Vocabulary → Comprehension → Writing. This creates a predictable ritual — kids know what to expect, parents know what each section measures.
threePartAssessmentStructure.consistency: Identical structure across all stories in the book. Same item count, same format, same layout.

mixedResponseTypes.description: Combines multiple-choice (items 1-18) with written response (items 19-20). The MC portion tests recognition; the writing portion tests recall and expression. This split prevents the assessment from being pure bubble-fill.

storySpecificVocabulary.description: Vocabulary words come directly from the story the child just read. The assessment tests whether they absorbed the words from reading context, not from rote memorization. Words are used in NEW sentences, not copied from the story.
storySpecificVocabulary.pattern: 6 vocab words per story, tested in novel sentence contexts

gradedLabeling.description: Grade badge in corner (e.g. 'Grade 2-1') makes it easy for parents to file and track progression. The '2-1' means second grade, first semester.

gaps.name: story-assessment
gaps.description: A three-section assessment tied to a specific reading selection: vocabulary (multiple-choice context sentences), comprehension (MC + short-answer), and writing (open response). Standardized format that repeats for every story. Currently no recipe for assessment/quiz/test generation in materials-studio.

notes: This is the assessment companion to the practice book pages (ref-2026-07-18-harcourt-trophies-2nd-practice-book). Carolyng specifically called out the three-section structure (vocab, comprehension, writing). The pages shown are from the Appendix section (A13-A44), covering two different stories. The consistent structure across stories is a key design pattern — it means the child learns the test format once and can focus on content rather than figuring out what to do.
